A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Copernicus-FM research. Their main texts and appendices A–E provide readable methods, equations, tables and figures that can be matched across additions, relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original component ablations, evaluations on 15 downstream tasks, and climate-regression experiments in Tables 2, 4 and 5, with further appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark and climate experiments and adds component-removal and variable-encoding comparisons in appendix Tables 8 and 10.

M1.justification: The spectral and variable hypernetworks, dynamic patch sizing, Fourier metadata integration, masked reconstruction and distillation objectives remain unchanged. The newly tested encoding alternatives are ablation comparators; global embedding generation retains the existing modality-averaging approach.

E1.justification: The pretraining modalities, 15 benchmark tasks and six climate-prediction variables remain unchanged. Copernicus-Embed-025deg extends embedding generation across existing pretraining data, without introducing another dataset or task used for training or evaluation.

E2.justification: New Table 10 evaluates Random hash and Spectroscopy against LLM-based variable encoding. The main benchmark comparators, including SoftCon, CROMA and DOFA, and the climate-regression baselines remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1 adds full-model-minus-component controls, extending the previous incremental ablation design under the retained ViT-Small, 10K-grid, 100-epoch setup. Existing benchmark splits, metrics and training settings remain unchanged; the BigEarthNet score revisions have no accompanying protocol explanation.

E4.justification: v3 adds systematic component-removal comparisons and tests whether language encoding offers benefits over hashing and spectroscopy. These extend existing incremental and metadata ablations. Table 8 partly reuses results from v1 Tables 2 and 10, so its contents are not entirely new analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-run means and standard deviations for benchmark and climate results, and Appendix C.4 specifies different random seeds. The added ablation tables retain the existing practice of reporting point estimates without uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 4 revises both BigEarthNet rows across all methods: Copernicus-FM's reported mAP changes from 83.3 to 77.9 on S1 and 84.6 to 79.0 on S2. SoftCon now leads S1 with 78.7. Tables 8 and 10 add ablation results, and Figures 6/34 add the global embedding map; most existing results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The Fourier-encoding definitions in Equations 1–2 and the mathematical description of the architecture are equivalent. No substantive derivations, assumptions, theorems or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: aligned Copernicus pretraining data, a flexible spectral/non-spectral foundation model, a 15-task benchmark and potential connections to climate modeling. Additional evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: The conclusion newly states the Sentinel-series and approximately one-year scope limitations and identifies native multimodal fusion and time-series processing as future work. Appendix B also explains the limitations of incremental ablations and discusses semantic and flexibility tradeoffs among variable encodings.

D1.justification: Table 10 newly specifies LLaMa-3.2-1B, while Appendix D.2 documents the embedding map's 721x1440x768 shape, 0.25-degree resolution and zero-filled empty ocean cells. The abstract changes its availability statement from code, datasets and models to code; Appendix E's planned releases and licenses remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 76 references and substantive related-work positioning are retained, including the relationship to DOFA and existing EO datasets and benchmarks. Changed citation backlinks reflect pagination rather than added or removed research.

P1.justification: Changes include removing the introduction's section roadmap, renaming a hypernetwork heading, refining appendix references, and adding localized ablation, embedding and limitations passages. The overall narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 gains a modality-count color scale, two ablation tables are added, and the new global embedding visualization appears in both Figures 6 and 34. Existing appendix displays are largely retained with resizing, relocation and renumbering; the basic layout remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: The additional controls in Tables 8 and 10 improve assessment of component and encoding choices, while explicit scope limitations and embedding-construction details improve transparency. These are focused gains over v1. The unexplained BigEarthNet score revisions remain a reporting weakness, and the main method and experimental coverage are unchanged.
